terms.gloss: the crop standing in the field; a cornfield
evidence: Cic. Or. 81: laetās esse segetēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: First a cornfield (Cato, Varro), then the crop growing in it; in that sense not frequent until after Augustus (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: grain; in the plural, the grain crops in the fields
evidence: Caes. B.G. 1.16.2: frūmenta in agrīs mātūra nōn erant

phrases.latin: segetēs runcārī, id est herbam ē segetibus expūrgārī
phrases.english: the crops are weeded, that is, the weeds are cleaned out of the crops

phrases.latin: sī bene flōruerint segetēs, erit ārea dīves; sī bene flōruerit vīnea, Bacchus erit
phrases.english: if the crops flower well, the threshing-floor will be rich; if the vineyard flowers well, there will be wine

sources: Lewis & Short: seges · Lewis & Short: frumentum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 166.
